description: Exercise and physical activity recommendations for menopause

entries.title: Regular Exercise Benefits
entries.description: Overall benefits of exercise during menopause
entries.content: Regular physical activity is one of the most important lifestyle interventions for managing menopause symptoms and maintaining health. Exercise helps with weight management, mood, sleep, bone health, cardiovascular health, and may reduce hot flash severity. Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate activity per week.
benefits: Reduces disease risk (diabetes, heart disease, cancer)
Improves balance and reduces fall risk
entries.recommendation: At least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity activity per week, plus strength training 2+ days per week

entries.title: Weight-Bearing Exercise for Bones
entries.description: Activities that strengthen bones and prevent osteoporosis
entries.content: Weight-bearing exercises, where your feet and legs support your weight, are essential for maintaining bone density and preventing osteoporosis after menopause. These activities stimulate bone formation and slow bone loss.
entries.recommendation: Include weight-bearing activity most days of the week
entries.note: Swimming and cycling are great for fitness but don't provide bone-strengthening benefits

entries.title: Resistance Training for Muscle and Bone
entries.description: Strength training to maintain muscle mass and bone density
entries.content: Resistance or strength training is crucial during menopause to maintain muscle mass (which naturally declines with age), strengthen bones, boost metabolism, and improve functional strength. It's as important as aerobic exercise.
entries.recommendation: 2-3 days per week, targeting all major muscle groups
benefits: Improves functional strength for daily activities
Improves balance and reduces fall risk
tips: Start with lighter weights and proper form
Allow rest days between sessions for same muscle groups

entries.title: Yoga and Tai Chi for Balance and Stress
entries.description: Mind-body exercises for flexibility, balance, and relaxation
entries.content: Yoga and tai chi combine gentle movement, stretching, balance, and mindfulness. They're excellent for improving flexibility, balance (reducing fall risk), reducing stress, and promoting relaxation during menopause.
benefits: Improves flexibility and range of motion
Enhances balance and coordination (reduces fall risk)
Can be adapted for all fitness levels
types: Yoga: Various styles from gentle (restorative, yin) to more active (vinyasa, power)
Tai chi: Slow, flowing movements with meditation
entries.recommendation: Include 1-3 times per week or as desired

entries.title: Cardiovascular Exercise for Heart Health
entries.description: Aerobic activities to strengthen heart and improve fitness
entries.content: Cardiovascular (aerobic) exercise strengthens your heart and lungs, improves circulation, helps manage weight, and reduces risk of heart disease - which increases after menopause. It also boosts mood and energy.
entries.intensity: Moderate intensity - can talk but not sing during activity
entries.recommendation: At least 150 minutes per week of moderate intensity, or 75 minutes of vigorous intensity

entries.title: Exercise Tips for Hot Flashes
entries.description: Managing exercise when experiencing hot flashes
entries.content: While regular exercise can help reduce hot flash severity over time, exercising can trigger hot flashes. These tips can help you stay active while managing symptoms.
tips: Exercise in cool environment (air conditioning, fan)
Layer clothing to remove as needed
Exercise earlier in day (not close to bedtime)
Have cool water or cold towel available
Don't let hot flashes stop you - benefits outweigh temporary discomfort
Consider swimming or water aerobics (naturally cooling)
entries.note: Regular exercise may reduce hot flash frequency and severity over time
